newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - July 23.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on July 23. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said after a meeting with President Suharto and the president of the Asian Development Bank that the government has no plans to change monetary policy. He said he was confident the foreign exchange market would improve on the back of the country's sound economic fundamentals.

Minister of Defense and Security Edi Sudradjat said that foreign countries should not interfere in Indonesia's internal affairs. In a written statement during the launch of the White Book on Indonesia's 1997 State Defence and Security Policy he said international relations should be built on mutual understanding of each country's sovereignty and integrity.

South African President Nelson Mandela met jailed East Timorese separatist leader Jose Alexandre 'Xanana' Gusmao at the Merdeka Palace during his visit last week, a senior pro-integration East Timor politician said. The meeting had taken place on July 15 and was held over dinner.

PT Caltex Pacific Indonesia has appealed to the government to reconsider its decision allowing state-owned oil company Pertamina to take over the Coastal Plains Pakanbaru (CPP) oil field in central Sumatra.
The Indonesian rupiah rose 65 points to 2,580 against the dollar on Tuesday from its previous position of 2,645 on Monday due to intervention of the Central Bank.

Interior Minister Yogie S. Memet said Megawati Sukarnoputri has to ask the police for permission if she wants to commemorate the first anniversary of the July 27 riots. He added though that if Megawati would hold a private gathering at her home she would be allowed to do so.
